title: Unsigned labelled-tail deletion correspondence
statement:
Let $I$ be a linearly ordered type, $p\in\mathbb N$, $n=p+2$, and $t:\operatorname{Fin}(n)\to I$. Use the stable sorts, partial sorts, and junction maps of [def-pc-alternating-cech-sorting-operators]. Write $q_{\sigma,\tau,a}=\operatorname{cechJunction}(\sigma,\tau,a)$ and $\delta_j=j.\operatorname{succAbove}$ for the increasing map omitting $j$. Let $O_t$ be the set of quadruples $(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$, with $\sigma,\tau\in S_n$, $a\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $r\in\operatorname{Fin}(n+1)$, such that $\sigma$ stably sorts $t$, $\tau$ partially sorts $\sigma$ with prefix length $a$, $q_{\sigma,\tau,a}(r)\ne\sigma(a)$, and $r\ge a$. Let $D_t$ be the set of quadruples $(j,\rho,b,\eta)$, with $j\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$, $\rho,\eta\in S_{n-1}$, $b\in\operatorname{Fin}(n-1)$, such that $\rho$ stably sorts $t\circ\delta_j$, $\eta$ partially sorts $\rho$ with prefix length $b$, and it is not the case that $t(j)<t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ or that $t(j)=t(\delta_j(\rho(b)))$ and $j<\delta_j(\rho(b))$. Then there exists an equivalence $e:O_t\simeq D_t$ such that for every $x=(\sigma,a,\tau,r)$, writing $e(x)=(j,\rho,b,\eta)$, there exists $k\in\operatorname{Fin}(n)$ with
$$k+1=r,\qquad \tau(k)=j,\qquad \tau\circ\delta_k=\delta_j\circ\eta,\qquad a=b,\qquad q_{\sigma,\tau,a}\circ\delta_r=\delta_j\circ q_{\rho,\eta,b}.$$
The position equality $a=b$ is an equality of natural-number values. This statement concerns only finite indices and maps; it has no coefficients or cochain values.

source.place: Tag 01FM, cohomology-equation-first-homotopy (20.23.6.1), omitted verification; unsigned tail-deletion part; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/01FM

proof.text: Order labels by the strict lexicographic order (t i,i). The stable sort is uniquely the increasing listing in this order. A partial sort is uniquely the prescribed prefix followed by the complementary labels in original-label order. For an outgoing index, q(a)=sigma(a), so the nonjunction condition and r>=a imply r>a. Put k=r-1 and j=tau(k). Since k>=a, j is outside the sorted prefix; since it differs from sigma(a), its stable rank is strictly after a. Remove j from sigma at its stable rank and from tau at k, renumbering surviving labels through the increasing map delta_j. The resulting permutations rho and eta have the same prefix length b=a, which lies in Fin(n-1) because there is a later stable rank. Rho is the stable sort of the restricted tuple, eta has its fixed prefix and increasing complementary tail, and j follows the retained junction in lexicographic order. Thus the incoming filter holds. Restricting tau gives tau composed with delta_k equals delta_j composed with eta. Checking positions up to a and after a separately in the junction formula gives q composed with delta_r equals delta_j composed with the restricted junction.

For an incoming index (j,rho,b,eta), the original junction label differs from j. The negated before condition therefore means j is strictly after that junction in lexicographic order. Insert j at its stable rank in the lifted stable sort rho, giving sigma. Lift the prefix of eta through delta_j and insert j into its increasing complementary tail at its original-label rank k, giving tau. Set a=b and r=k+1. The prefix is unchanged, k>=a, and tau(k)=j differs from sigma(a), so the outgoing filter holds. Restriction removes exactly the inserted positions; conversely reinsertion recovers the original stable and tail orders. The two operations are inverse because each order gives a unique insertion rank. This yields e and every asserted identity. When a=n-1 the outgoing filter is empty, since the only unused tail label is the junction. For p=0, the construction involves two original labels and one surviving label. Equal t-values cause no ties in the lexicographic label order; an empty I admits no input tuple.

theorem cechTailDeletionCorrespondence {I : Type v} [LinearOrder I] (p : ℕ)
    (t : Fin (p + 2) → I) :
    ∃ e : cechTailOutgoingIndex p t ≃ cechTailIncomingIndex p t,
      ∀ x, ∃ k : Fin (p + 2),
        k.val + 1 = x.val.2.2.2.val ∧
        x.val.2.2.1 k = (e x).val.1 ∧
        (∀ z, x.val.2.2.1 (k.succAbove z) =
          (e x).val.1.succAbove ((e x).val.2.2.2 z)) ∧
        x.val.2.1.val = (e x).val.2.2.1.val ∧
        cechJunction x.val.1 x.val.2.2.1 x.val.2.1 ∘ x.val.2.2.2.succAbove =
          (e x).val.1.succAbove ∘
            cechJunction (e x).val.2.1 (e x).val.2.2.2 (e x).val.2.2.1
